# wing

wing is a Zig CLI for Confluent Schema Registry and JSON Schema. It composes
with kite, a Kafka CLI, using one JSON record per line.

## Stable contract

- `wing read` resolves Confluent schema IDs, validates consumed kite JSON
  records, and emits records with schema ID headers/prefixes removed.
- `wing write [REF] [--fit]` validates records, applies schema-directed
  fitting when requested, and adds the selected GUID schema header.
- `wing push [TOPIC]` lints and registers a JSON Schema. `--check` lints
  without registering; `--meta` reads/writes registry metadata envelopes.
- `wing get REF` prints schema text; `--meta` prints
  `{topic,version,id,guid,compat,schema,references,metadata,ruleSet}`.
- `wing ls [TOPIC]`, `wing rm REF -y`, `wing registry list|set|init`, and
  `wing update [VERSION]` manage registry schemas and configuration.
- Record input is kite `--json`: one JSON object per line with `value`
  required. Strings represent bytes; object/array values use their source JSON.
- stdout is data and stderr is diagnostics. Validation pointers are plain JSON
  Pointers, with the root represented by the empty string.
- Exit codes: `0` success; `1` usage/configuration/registry/tool failure;
  `2` invalid records/schema or failed checks; `130` SIGINT/SIGTERM.
- Configure via `--registry`, `SCHEMA_REGISTRY_URL`, or `wing.yaml`.
  `@NAME` selects a named registry for one invocation.
- `--errors=json` writes structured diagnostic lines to stderr; `-q` suppresses
  summaries; `-v` adds provenance and fitting changes.
- Per-record diagnostics, notes, and summaries are prefixed `wing read:` or
  `wing write:`. Missing write schema uses:
  `no schema for this record; pass a topic (wing write TOPIC) or keep the schema field from wing read`.
- `wing push` without a topic requires `--check` for offline linting; empty
  stdin reports `wing push: no schema on stdin`.
- Compatibility failures identify the subject, latest version, and
  compatibility level, with JSON Pointer paths in text and JSON diagnostics.

See README.md for commands, options, configuration precedence, and pipelines.
